clue.text: Today, after end of blizzards, phone for appropriate vehicle?

indicators.note: the word for today is placed after the letter from blizzards
the end of a word is its final letter, so only the last letter of blizzards is used

parts.note: now means at the present time, today
a mobile is a mobile phone, a cellphone

explanation.surface: Someone stuck after a blizzard rings for a suitable vehicle to get about.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition leans on the snowy surface: after blizzards this is just the right vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorised sledge for travelling over snow is the fitting transport once blizzards have passed.

clue.text: Separate stock

definitions.meaning: to separate solids from liquid, as through a sieve or filter
stock as a breed or line of animals or plants

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to sieve or filter and a breed or variety of plant or animal.

clue.text: Alternative arrangement for trial

parts.note: or introduces an alternative
a deal is an arrangement or agreement

explanation.surface: A different arrangement is proposed in place of a court trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternative arrangement' sounds like an anagram signal, but it is two plain pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A painful, testing experience is a trial; medieval trial by ordeal is the original sense.

clue.text: Garment maker: working man, clothier, at start of Row

indicators.note: working means at work, set in motion, so the letters are reshaped
the start is the opening letter of the word Row

explanation.surface: A clothes maker is a working man, a clothier, on Savile Row.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is MAN CLOTHIER AT plus R, the start of Row.
explanation.definitionFit: A merchant tailor was a tailor who also sold cloth, so someone who makes garments.

clue.text: Wife quite possibly in prison

parts.note: a bride is a newly married wife
well means quite possibly, as in 'it may well rain'

explanation.surface: Someone's wife may quite possibly be in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridewell was a London prison, and the name became a general word for a house of correction.
explanation.definitionFit: A bridewell is an old word for a jail or house of correction, after the London one.

clue.text: Short modern drink

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: latter means more recent or modern, as in its latter days

explanation.surface: A quick, trendy coffee drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' suggests a short drink or espresso; it trims the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A milky espresso coffee is a drink found in any café.

clue.text: Move through water so well in motorboat, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the words so, well, in, motorboat

explanation.surface: Someone praises a motorboat for cutting through the water so well.
explanation.definitionFit: Propelling yourself through water with arms and legs is the everyday sense of the verb.

clue.text: Insect in that wine put out

indicators.note: put out means disturbed, so the letters of the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insect lands in that wine, which has been set out.
explanation.definitionFit: A termite is commonly called this, though it is not truly an ant; it is an insect.

clue.text: Old musician, male in street on left

parts.note: re means on or concerning

explanation.surface: A man on the left of the street is an old musician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' here gives its own letters rather than signalling insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval singer or travelling performer of songs was such a musician.

clue.text: Displaying trophy on table somewhere warm

parts.note: airing an opinion or item is displaying it
a cup is a trophy
a board is a table, as in bed and board

explanation.surface: A trophy is displayed on a table in some warm room.
explanation.walkthrough: An airing cupboard is a heated cupboard, usually with the water tank, where British households dry and warm linen.
explanation.definitionFit: A heated cupboard housing a hot water tank is a warm spot for drying linen.

clue.text: Clear, the Queen's jockey

parts.note: to rid a place of something is to clear it
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: A racing report that the Queen's jockey has been cleared.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey is someone who rides horses in races, so a horse rider.

clue.text: During teaching, sixth sense acquired

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'
tuition is teaching or instruction

explanation.surface: A student picks up a sixth sense while being taught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acquired' is a link: a sixth sense acquired in tuition is the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A sixth sense is a hunch or instinctive knowing without reasoning, which is what this word names.

clue.text: Book one vehicle in front of house by base

indicators.note: the vehicle comes in front of the house abbreviation in the word

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a van is a vehicle
e is the base of natural logarithms in mathematics

explanation.surface: Someone books a van to park outside a house near a base.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Book' looks like a verb (reserve a vehicle) but is a noun: Walter Scott's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivanhoe is a novel by Sir Walter Scott, so an example of a book.

clue.text: Marked papers in the course of meeting

indicators.note: in the course of means within, so the papers go inside the meeting

parts.note: an event, such as a race meeting, is a meeting
ID, identification, is papers you carry

explanation.surface: Papers marked during a meeting, like documents annotated at a committee.
explanation.definitionFit: Something marked, as in a marked improvement, is plain and obvious to see.

clue.text: Mind dope

definitions.meaning: mind as the faculty of thinking and understanding, brainpower
dope as slang for information, the inside gen, as spies gather

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both mental ability and secret information, as in military intelligence or the dope on someone.

clue.text: Story about motorway illumination becomes focus of attention

indicators.note: about means around, so the story goes round the motorway letter

parts.note: a lie is a story, a fib
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
light is illumination

explanation.surface: A tale about motorway lighting becomes the centre of attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the public eye, the centre of attention, comes from old stage lighting.

clue.text: Student leaving ahead of time to catch young lady's agent

indicators.note: to catch means to hold something inside, so the young lady goes within
leaving means the student letter departs from the word

parts.note: early means ahead of time
L, the learner plate, stands for student
a miss is a young lady

explanation.surface: A student leaves early to meet a young woman's representative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes L from EARLY, giving EARY, which then catches MISS.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission is an agent acting for someone.

clue.text: Article supporting well-known landlord

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits beneath the other

parts.note: public means well-known, as in a public figure
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article backing a famous landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: A landlord in Britain is also the keeper of a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a pub landlord, the keeper of a public house, is called this.

clue.text: Disgusting mum, pylons out in Greek national park

indicators.note: disgusting suggests the letters are upset and turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: Mum is appalled by pylons put up in a Greek national park.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disgusting' reads as an adjective for mum, but it is the anagram signal for MUM PYLONS OUT.
explanation.definitionFit: The mountain home of the Greek gods is also the centre of a Greek national park.

clue.text: Local controversy, a burial mound

parts.note: a local is a British pub, so a bar
a row is a quarrel or controversy

explanation.surface: A local dispute over an ancient burial mound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is a noun: the British word for a neighbourhood pub.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancient tumulus heaped over a grave is called this.

clue.text: Detour near narrow defile

parts.note: by means near, as in close by
a pass is a narrow route through mountains

explanation.surface: A diversion avoids a narrow mountain gorge nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: A road round a town or obstacle is a detour that goes around it.

clue.text: Forays in south by Confederates

indicators.note: by means beside, so the confederates come next to the south letter

parts.note: allies are confederates, partners in a league

explanation.surface: A Civil War picture: Confederate raids in the South.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Confederates' evokes the American South but just means allies.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorties or sudden raids out of a defended position are forays.

clue.text: Outburst from Surrey's opener staggered Oval

indicators.note: the opener is the first in the order, so the first letter of Surrey's
staggered means reeling, so the letters of the ground's name are jumbled

explanation.surface: Surrey's opening batsman staggers the Oval crowd with an outburst of strokes.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is Surrey's cricket ground in London; 'opener' is also a cricket word.
explanation.definitionFit: A burst of firing or of words is a salvo, a sudden outburst.

clue.text: Where one may find 'The Borrowers'?

parts.note: The Borrowers is a children's novel, but borrowers are also the people who take out books, found at a lending institution

explanation.surface: A question about where to locate Mary Norton's children's book.
explanation.walkthrough: The title points at the book; the joke is that borrowers, the members taking out books, are found there.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowers of books are found at a lending building of books, and so is the novel.

clue.text: Charon cracked on, being part of relay

indicators.note: cracked means broken apart, so the name Charon is rearranged

parts.note: on is the leg side in cricket, the half of the field behind the batsman's legs

explanation.surface: Charon, ferryman of the dead, pressed on with his share of a relay.
explanation.walkthrough: Leg and on are the same side of a cricket field.
explanation.definitionFit: The final stage of a relay race, run by the strongest runner, is a named stage of it.

clue.text: Vessel from Altamira or Tampico

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words Altamira or Tampico

explanation.surface: A ship sailing from one of two Latin American or Spanish ports.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' suggests a ship sailing from a port; it is the blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The main artery carrying blood from the heart is a blood vessel.

clue.text: Pull bovine animal, holding tail of bison

indicators.note: holding means the animal contains the next letter inside it

parts.note: a yak is a long-haired bovine animal of Tibet

indicators.note: the tail is the final letter of the word bison

explanation.surface: Tugging a cow-like beast along by gripping a bison's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a sudden hard tug is to jerk or pull.

clue.text: Consequently hut damaged on fells, a range of hills

parts.note: so means consequently or therefore

indicators.note: damaged suggests the hut is knocked about into a new order

parts.note: fells and downs are both upland hills

explanation.surface: A hut on the fells was damaged, so the hills are named.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalk hill range across Sussex and Hampshire in southern England bears this name.
